questions.question: Q: Name the five types of stimulus used in dance choreography.

points.text: Visual, auditory, kinaesthetic, ideational and literary.

questions.question: Q: Give an example of a visual stimulus and explain how it could inspire movement.

points.text: A painting of a stormy sea could inspire swirling, expansive movements with sudden changes in dynamics to represent crashing waves.

questions.question: Q: How does an ideational stimulus differ from a literary stimulus?

points.text: An ideational stimulus is a concept or theme (e.g. loneliness), whereas a literary stimulus is based on specific words (e.g. a poem about loneliness).

questions.question: Q: Why might a choreographer choose to combine more than one type of stimulus?

points.text: Combining stimuli can create richer, more layered choreography — for example, using both a visual image and a piece of music to inspire contrasting movement qualities.

questions.question: Q: Explain how a kinaesthetic stimulus could be used to create movement material.

points.text: A kinaesthetic stimulus such as the feeling of tension in the shoulders could be explored and developed into movement phrases that show struggle or restriction.
